title: US Destroys Five Iranian Oil Tankers as Tehran Missiles Rain on Jordan, UK Sanctions West Bank Settlements and Israel Shuts Its Consulate
subhead: The US-Iran war lurched back toward open hostilities with the destruction of five Iranian tankers and a missile barrage on US targets in Jordan, while London's sanctions on West Bank settlements triggered a furious Israeli response and a diplomatic rupture.

sections.heading: US-Iran War Escalates: Tankers Destroyed, Missiles on Jordan
sections.body:
The US military said it destroyed five Iranian oil tankers on Tuesday in response to the latest attacks on its warships, and Tehran hit back at American targets in Jordan, according to AP. Jordan's military said its air defenses intercepted 18 ballistic missiles launched toward its territory, with two others falling in unpopulated areas and no reported casualties. The exchange marks the latest burst of back-and-forth strikes in a war now more than six months old.

The tanker strikes follow Saturday's destruction of three Iranian oil tankers after the Revolutionary Guards tried to attack a US aircraft carrier and destroyer with ballistic missiles. Washington has warned it would, if necessary, destroy Iran's limited and exposed oil fleet. The Trump administration also imposed fresh sanctions on more than two dozen Iranian commercial and private airlines plus foreign cargo providers, part of its Operation Economic Outcast campaign. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that anyone doing business with Iran's remaining airlines risks being cut off from the global financial system. Brent crude briefly climbed as high as $99.46 a barrel, according to AP.
sections.whyItMatters: The US is now systematically destroying Iran's oil fleet while tightening the economic noose, and Iran is responding with missile barrages on a key US ally. With Brent near $100 and both sides seeking control of the Strait of Hormuz, the war shows no off-ramp and rising energy costs are becoming a political problem for Washington ahead of the November midterms.

sections.heading: UK Sanctions West Bank Settlements, Israel Shuts Consulate
sections.body:
The UK announced sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, with Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband accusing Israel's government of turning a blind eye to the ethnic cleansing of Palestinians by settlers, the BBC reports. The measures, launched alongside France and Canada, will ban settlement goods and target companies and individuals providing services for settlement expansion, with a new comprehensive sanctions regime to follow over the next six to nine months.

Israel's Foreign Minister Gideon Saar responded furiously, calling the accusation an outrageous lie and announcing counter-measures including shutting the UK's consulate in East Jerusalem and banning 11 UK MPs, including Jeremy Corbyn and Diane Abbott, from entering Israel. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the measures were aimed not at the Israeli people but in support of the two-state solution. The BBC's Paul Adams described British-Israeli relations as at their lowest ebb in decades.
sections.whyItMatters: A major Western ally has formally adopted the position that Israel's occupation of the West Bank is unlawful and is backing it with sanctions, aligning with the 2024 ICJ advisory opinion. The rupture with Israel over settlements signals a realignment in Western policy toward the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, even as the US-Iran war rages.

sections.heading: US-Canada Trade War Widens Beyond Tariffs
sections.body:
The United States is banning dairy products, most alcoholic beverages and motorcycles from Canada, the White House said Tuesday, in the latest escalation of the trade war between the two nations, according to AP. The ban takes effect in three weeks and comes after Canada imposed retaliatory tariffs on about $20 billion worth of US goods earlier the same day.

Prime Minister Mark Carney has said US demands could hollow out key Canadian industries and limit the country's independence, while Trump's threats to Canadian sovereignty have rallied the public behind him. AP reported that so far Trump's pressure has backfired, strengthening support for Carney rather than forcing concessions. The dispute has moved well beyond tariffs into direct import bans on specific sectors.
sections.whyItMatters: The world's two largest trading partners are now banning specific goods outright rather than just taxing them, a qualitative escalation of a dispute that has already rattled North American supply chains. Trump's pressure appears to be consolidating Canadian nationalism behind Carney rather than extracting concessions.

sections.heading: Houthis Strike Saudi Cities and Energy Facilities, Riyadh Vows Response
sections.body:
Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi movement attacked energy facilities and civilian infrastructure in four south-western Saudi cities with dozens of drones and missiles, injuring 73 people, Saudi authorities told the BBC. The strikes on Abha, Khamis Mushait, Jazan and Najran caused fires at oil facilities and a temporary halt in some operations, according to Saudi Arabia's military and energy ministry.

The Saudi-led coalition said it would respond to the dangerous escalation, while the Houthis said the attacks were retaliation for more than 120 Saudi air strikes on Yemeni provinces over the past three days. The informal ceasefire that held for four years began to unravel in July, and heavy fighting has raged on Yemen's south-western coast since Thursday as the Houthis launched an offensive toward the Bab al-Mandab Strait, leaving more than 300 dead and 18,500 displaced.
sections.whyItMatters: The Red Sea route has become critical for Saudi oil shipments because the US-Iran war has effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz. Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure now threaten the kingdom's ability to export at all, and Riyadh's promised military response risks opening a second front in the broader regional war.

sections.heading: Russia Strikes Kyiv TV Station as Capital Attacks Intensify
sections.body:
A Russian drone struck the headquarters of the Ukrainian TV channel We Are Ukraine in Kyiv, injuring at least five people as journalists broadcast live, President Volodymyr Zelensky said, per the BBC. Zelensky called the daytime attack a new page in Russian degradation, and the channel said footage confirmed it was a deliberate attack targeting journalists. At least five people were killed in overnight and daytime Russian strikes on Kyiv, with a separate attack on a passenger train in southern Ukraine killing a female employee.

The strikes came despite an agreement by both countries to halt attacks on each other's capitals for three days while US envoys visited Moscow and Kyiv over the weekend. According to BBC Verify, Kyiv is suffering more daily air raid alerts than at any time since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022. In Russia, buildings were struck in the city of Saratov during a Ukrainian drone attack.
sections.whyItMatters: The collapse of the brief capital-strikes pause shows the limits of the diplomatic channel opened by the US envoy visits. Russia's targeting of a live-broadcasting newsroom is a deliberate strike on the media, and the intensity of attacks on Kyiv signals Moscow is not de-escalating despite the diplomatic overtures.

sections.heading: Argentina Files Criminal Case Over Falklands Oil Drilling
sections.body:
Argentina said it will file criminal charges against oil company Navitas Petroleum for operating in seas off the Falkland Islands, the BBC reports. The move came days after President Javier Milei said he would sanction oil companies drilling in the British overseas territory, describing drilling there as a clear and urgent danger to Argentine sovereignty.

Milei dismissed the 2013 referendum in which 99.8% of islanders voted to remain British, arguing they had no legitimate right to self-determination on land he says was usurped. Navitas, listed in Tel Aviv, holds a 65% stake in the Sea Lion oil project. Britain's Foreign Office Minister Kirsty McNeill insisted there could be no doubt about London's commitment to the Falkland Islanders, saying the future of the islands is for islanders to determine.
sections.whyItMatters: Milei's shift from pro-UK diplomacy to criminal prosecution of oil companies marks a sharp escalation of the Falklands dispute, targeting the commercial foundation of the territory's economy. With the US-Iran war straining global energy markets, the dispute over South Atlantic oil adds another flashpoint to the scramble for energy security.

bottomLine: The US-Iran war lurched back toward open hostilities as Washington destroyed five Iranian tankers and Tehran fired 18 missiles at US targets in Jordan, with Brent crude pushing toward $100 and no off-ramp in sight. In parallel, the UK's sanctions on West Bank settlements triggered a diplomatic rupture with Israel, the US-Canada trade war escalated into outright import bans, and the Houthis struck Saudi energy infrastructure as the Red Sea front intensifies. The day's developments point to a world where multiple overlapping conflicts — the Gulf war, the Red Sea, Ukraine, and Western trade disputes — are all escalating simultaneously, with energy security and alliance cohesion under mounting strain.
